text: just way too much added to the game over time, genuinely at this point it's impossible to actually get anywhere because of symbol bloat. i used to be able to freely enjoy synergies and fail because i actually MADE mistakes, and now all i can do is suffer the worst luck in the world by getting 70 different non-synergizing symbols, to the point i even failed the very first payment several times because i got way too many weak symbols that couldn't pay back their slot use and had literally no synergy offered, which for reference the first payment is ONLY 25 COINS.

In principle this is a decent roguelike deckbuilder or card (slot) drafting game, and I appreciate that it served as an inspiration for Balatro, but ultimately I find it painful to play.

The drafting part of the game is genuinely challenging and would offer an interesting skill-based challenge, if only the UI were better. But the menus are a mess (e.g. I only learned after playing that there were keyboard shortcuts), the drafting of cards (slot symbols) and items doesn't give you any useful information regarding what kinds of cards and items you already have, many of the card and item tooltips are walls of text or otherwise hard to parse, and the "library view" is frankly hideous to look at and a terrible way to present this information.

As a result, the core activity in the game - the drafting - feels needlessly frustrating and time-consuming. I can easily imagine a version of this game that presented usefully actionable information (e.g. "here's how many fruit/aquatic/mineral/human cards you have") and made the drafting a joy instead of a pain, but unfortunately that's not what we got here.

Apart from that, the design of cards and items is also frustrating in that most of them are very narrow, e.g. there are items that support rabbits, or wolves, or humans, or thieves, or whatever, and if you don't have any of these cards, then the item is useless. This makes many draft choices very boring skips. Something I appreciate in other roguelike deckbuilders like Slay the Spire

Luck Be a Landlord wasn’t what I expected, and it ended up not being very fun for me. The game is built around a slot machine system where you add symbols and hope for good rolls to pay rent, but in practice it feels very repetitive. Most of the time you’re just watching the screen spin, waiting for something mildly interesting to happen. Even though I enjoy gambling-style mechanics, this didn’t scratch that itch. It felt more passive than engaging, and the novelty wore off quickly.

The entire time I played this, I never found myself enjoying it at all. I'm really not sure what's supposed to be enjoyable about this game, as I love roguelikes, RNG is cool, but this is just... really boring.

If you enjoy slot machines, you might think Luck be a Landlord is fun. I didn't find the game very engaging or fun. I had higher hopes since this is the game that inspired Balatro, but ultimately I just couldn't find myself having a good time playing this game. Everything feels too random, and upgrades don't seem to matter much. I get that the goal is to craft synergies, but even then the slot machine mechanic makes everything feel too RNG for my taste.

I got this because this is one of those roguelikes that gets referenced a lot and is often brought up as a baseline point of comparison, similar to [i]Slay the Spire[/i] or [i]Hades[/i], like this is an origin point for this particular style of gameplay which obviously evokes a slot machine but is not in practice very much like one. 

I think I appreciate having it under my belt as a point of reference but since I've played a couple of games that develop on this baseline mechanic I find this one pretty lacking. Mostly I feel that the game doesn't really give you enough control over the RNG and as a result games feel like they're impossible to win or you've won like a full dozen or more spins before you make your final payment. It's just rough, I think rather than playing more of this, I'd rather go back and put more hours into [i]Crop Rotation[/i] which is similar but more polished in every regard.

Wish I could give a neutral recommendation. It's ok. The strategy is not as deep as I hoped - rather than being able to focus on a particular strategy, you really just need to grab things as you see them and hobble together enough points to get through. 

Doing achievements feels forced rather than exciting. While some come naturally, many of them require you to get to endless mode and just grind through different spins until you get what you need. This is not fun. As a comparison, I'm still trying to get my last two achievements on Balatro and they have all felt exciting and fun to pursue and get.

There's also a huge oversight with the spin countdown to rent due as well as the amount of upcoming rent due. You see it when you finish a spin, but nowhere else. This should be on the screen at all times. 

The Balatro developer said this was a major inspiration for Balatro and I can see the inspiration but am glad that Balatro took it to an entirely new level. I know I've been negative here but the initial game (which took me under five hours to beat) was enjoyable and a decent way to pass time. I just thought there would be more game that would open up and though a few things are added as you pass through different levels, the base game is pretty much the same. 

I bought it at full price and regret it. If it was $5, I'd be happy enough, so I can recommend it on sale if you like this type of RNG heavy, luck-based games, but can't recommend at full price, particularly since most

I understand why people might like this but I just found it kinda boring. I saw that Balatro was inspired by this game an figured I'd give it a try. I like slots in other games like PSO2 and I think my main problem is you don't get the satisfaction of actually lining things up. Every icon on the screen gives you coins, and many icons interact with each other which is a great idea. Also having to pick a new icon to add after EVERY spin really breaks the pace of the game for me. You spend more time reading the icon effects than actually spinning the slot machine.

If you had to choose tiles to maximize interactions between matches instead of just maximizing payout I think it would be a lot more interesting.

I kind of hate to say it but I can't reccomend it.
No win has felt rewarding and no loss has felt like my fault.
The game lacks depth - and sure, the point of a roguelike is that you can't just [b] choose [/b] any build you want per se, but you could spend [b] painstaking [/b] amounts of time waiting for that one symbol central to your strat. The more fun a strategy or build would've been, the less likely it's you'll actually get to pull it off, so you'll probably be spending the most time playing with the same items. There's just not enough depth.
The apartment floors concept is very poorly executed and each level is only marginally harder than the previous, often unnoticeably. The "bossfight" doesn't help replayability either, as it gets old pretty much instantly.

The game lacks depth. There is extremely limited player input outside of the deckbuilding aspect, as it is based on slot machines. Difficulty is very binary too; either you were offered enough synergistic cards for you to win, or you were not. Replay value is quite low since each "fight" is the same - Meet the required score, or lose. Outside of the "boss" there are no fights with extra conditions to make you reconsider the way you are building your deck. Some of the cards have interesting effects, but since you have no control of how they are played - again, it's a slot machine - rather than feeling a sense of accomplishment for beating a tough fight, you just feel like you got lucky. Beyond that, the game's "endless mode" simply removes the "fighting an enemy" aspect by no longer requiring you to beat a certain score, so the only point of it is to get achievements for the sake of completionism. 

Outside of gameplay, the soundtrack and graphics are nothing to write home about. They are about on par with a 2000's era flash game. They do not detract from the game, but they also do not add much. The game's "story" is sub-par - you are only fighting because the gameplay requires it, rather than the "characters" being compelling. I think that improving the writing and adding some sort of level design to the background as you progress through the game would go a long way towards improving it.

Overall, while the game is not awful, a lack of polish makes it hard for me to recommen

Sadly, I can't recommend it. There's some strategy in choosing which symbols to add to your reel after every spin, but the near complete inability to influence which types of symbols show up mean that you have very little meaningful ability to guide the course of your game other than making what's usually just the least bad decision.

If it's priced at $2-3, it might be worth it to kill some time, but as it stands now I really can't recommend it above that price.
